role_summary: Owns design surface end-to-end for a Series-B B2B SaaS in product analytics. Ships shipped product across web app + onboarding + dashboards. Works with PMs and engineering on weekly cadence; drives a small design system library used across the team.

capability_areas.name: Information density
capability_areas.description: Designs dense data surfaces well — charts, tables, query builders, dashboards — without losing scannability or hierarchy.

capability_areas.name: Design systems
capability_areas.description: Builds and maintains a small-but-well-loved design system. Tokens, components, governance. Comfortable shipping it as the only designer in a 5-engineer pod.

capability_areas.name: Onboarding flow craft
capability_areas.description: Has shipped onboarding flows for technical products. Knows the difference between 'we explained the feature' and 'the user reached aha-moment in <5 minutes'.

depth_distinction.builder_definition: Owns the surface end-to-end including governance. Ships shipped product. Maintains a small design system library used across the team. Comfortable being the only designer in a 5-engineer pod.
depth_distinction.user_definition: Consumes existing design systems without authoring. Ships polish on top of patterns someone else built. Workmanlike rather than load-bearing.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: Borderline = consumed-then-extended a design system. Senior IC who can occasionally do governance work but isn't the system's primary owner.

non_fit_patterns.label: marketing-only portfolio
non_fit_patterns.why_not: no shipped product evidence; the work is brand and editorial, not B2B SaaS interface design

non_fit_patterns.label: agency-only portfolio
non_fit_patterns.why_not: all client deliverables, no in-house product ownership; lacks the design-system + onboarding-flow craft we need at this stage

non_fit_patterns.label: consumer-only portfolio
non_fit_patterns.why_not: consumer aesthetics + flows don't carry into dense B2B information surfaces; the visual language is differently tuned

principles.name: Visual hierarchy
principles.description: How clearly the work guides attention across dense data surfaces. Primary actions distinct from secondary; data legible at scan distance.

anchors.bad: No discernible hierarchy. Every element competes equally for attention.
anchors.okay: Hierarchy present but weak. Distinctions between primary and secondary elements require effort to read.
anchors.good: Clear hierarchy. Primary, secondary, and tertiary elements visually distinct; the eye lands on the intended focal point.
anchors.excellent: Hierarchy is purposeful and confident. Each layer serves a deliberate communication purpose.

principles.name: Typographic refinement
principles.description: Typography as a first-class material. Number formatting, table type, label sizing — the small things that distinguish a polished SaaS surface from a workmanlike one.

anchors.bad: Type undifferentiated or default. No evidence of intentional typeface selection, sizing, or rhythm.
anchors.okay: Type consistent without precision. Choices workable but not load-bearing for the work's identity.
anchors.good: Type intentional and well-set. Kerning, leading, and pairing reflect craft; typography carries voice without effort.
anchors.excellent: Typography is a primary expressive material. Decisive type choices, micro-typography precision, and editorial restraint.

principles.name: Compositional balance
principles.description: Spatial relationships across the canvas. Negative space as a positive material; consistent rhythm across screens.

anchors.bad: Composition cluttered or arbitrary. Elements feel placed rather than arranged.
anchors.okay: Composition workable but predictable. Default grid behavior; no compositional ambition.
anchors.good: Composition considered. Rhythm and balance intentional; negative space used as a positive material.
anchors.excellent: Composition is the design itself. Tension, asymmetry, and pacing deployed with intent.

principles.name: Color system coherence
principles.description: How color choices relate as a system. Palette discipline, chromatic relationships, and the emotional / functional purpose of color in dense data contexts.

anchors.bad: Color incidental or chaotic. No discernible palette discipline.
anchors.okay: Color works but isn't a system. Choices workable; coherence approximate.
anchors.good: Color systematic. Palette clearly defined; relationships between colors intentional.
anchors.excellent: Color is a structural material. Palette has perspective and decisiveness.

principles.name: Conceptual strength
principles.description: Whether the work expresses an idea beyond its surface. Sharp underlying concept the visual choices serve.

anchors.bad: No discernible concept beneath the surface.
anchors.okay: Concept present but generic. The frame is recognizable; not particularly its own.
anchors.good: Concept sharp and the visual choices serve it consistently.
anchors.excellent: Concept original and the execution makes the concept inevitable.

principles.name: Craft execution
principles.description: Fit, finish, and the absence of avoidable errors. Spacing precision, edge treatment, alignment discipline.

anchors.bad: Visible craft errors. Misaligned elements, low-resolution assets, or mistreated edges signal indifference.
anchors.okay: Craft acceptable. Few errors but not particularly precise.
anchors.good: Craft clean. Spacing, alignment, and finish precise; the work reads as intentional throughout.
anchors.excellent: Craft is at the limit of what the medium allows.

hard_reject_patterns: layout-only portfolio with no shipped product
all client work no in-house product ownership
